Since `topology` is an EXPERIMENTAL genre (per the router table), I've kept the figure minimal and structural — ids and short labels only, with `class` carrying the primary/backup distinction so it survives as text, not just colour.

```figdown
# FigDown — figures as text. Spec: https://github.com/FigDown/figdown
figdown 0.1 topology
title "Branch office WAN uplinks"

class primary "Primary WAN uplink" stroke=#16a34a
class backup "Backup WAN uplink" stroke=#dc2626 style=dashed

node access1 "Access Switch 1"
node access2 "Access Switch 2"
node branch "Branch Router"
node hubprimary "Regional Hub (Primary)"
node hubbackup "Regional Hub (Backup)"

edge access1 branch
edge access2 branch
edge branch hubprimary class=primary
edge branch hubbackup class=backup
```

Notes:
- `topology` sits in the right-hand ("experimental constructs") column of the genre router, so this document trades the compatibility promise of `block`/`bitfield`/`table` for topology's own vocabulary — stated here rather than left implicit.
- The two hub routers are modeled as distinct nodes (`hubprimary`, `hubbackup`) per the source description of diverse paths, not as one node with two labels.
- Link roles (primary vs. backup) are carried by `class`, not by colour alone, so the meaning survives even if the render is viewed without the legend.
- Run `node build-svg.js branch-wan-uplinks.fd` to produce the SVG, then embed with the standard `source:` footer pointing at this `.fd`.
